mean: enthusiasm that fades almost as soon as it starts

use.how: Noun phrase, usually after 是、只有、就是 or 又是: 他学什么都是三分钟热度。 Said of a person's short-lived keenness for a hobby, plan or resolution.

near.diff: 虎头蛇尾 is a strong start and a weak finish of one task; 三分钟热度 is a person's habit of losing interest quickly.

cue: Your friend buys a guitar, a gym card and a set of paints in one month, and has given up on all of them by the next. What do you say about her?

ctx.s: 他学什么都是{三分钟热度}，从来坚持不下去。
ctx.en: Whatever he takes up, his enthusiasm dies in no time; he never sticks with anything.

ctx.s: 你上个月说要学日语，现在书都不翻了，又是{三分钟热度}吧？
ctx.en: Last month you said you'd learn Japanese and now you don't even open the book. Lost interest already?

ctx.s: 孩子想学钢琴，我们怕他只有{三分钟热度}，先租了一台试试。
ctx.en: Our son wants to learn the piano; we were afraid his keenness wouldn't last, so we rented one to try first.

ctx.s: “这次我一定每天跑步！”“得了吧，你就是{三分钟热度}。”
ctx.en: "This time I'll definitely run every day!" "Oh, come on, you'll lose interest in a few days."

ctx.s: 很多人新年定了计划，可惜大多是{三分钟热度}，二月就忘了。
ctx.en: Lots of people make New Year resolutions, but most of that enthusiasm fizzles out and is forgotten by February.

ctx.s: 网上的热点来得快去得也快，大家对什么都只有{三分钟的热度}。
ctx.en: Online trends come and go fast; people never stay interested in anything for long.

bad.s: 他对工作很有{三分钟热度}，每天都加班。
bad.en: (meant: he is very passionate about his work and works overtime every day)
bad.why: It does not mean passion; it says the enthusiasm will not last, so it cannot describe steady dedication.

bad.s: 微波炉{三分钟热度}，饭就热好了。
bad.en: (meant: three minutes in the microwave and the food is hot)
bad.why: It is only used figuratively about a person's interest fading, never about heating something for three minutes.

mean: just as bad as each other, nothing to choose between them
lit: half a jin and eight liang: on the old scale of sixteen liang to the jin, the same weight

use.how: Predicate after two people or things: 你们俩半斤八两。 Usually says both are equally poor or equally to blame; can be wry about oneself.

near.diff: 不相上下 is a neutral 'evenly matched' that suits praise; 半斤八两 suggests both are equally bad.

cue: Two brothers each blame the other for the mess in their room, and you know they are both equally messy. How do you sum them up?

ctx.s: 你们俩{半斤八两}，谁也别笑话谁。
ctx.en: You two are as bad as each other, so neither of you should laugh at the other.

ctx.s: 他说我做饭难吃，其实他的手艺跟我{半斤八两}。
ctx.en: He says my cooking is awful, but his is no better than mine.

ctx.s: “这两家公司哪家服务好一点？”“{半斤八两}，都挺差的。”
ctx.en: "Which of these two companies has better service?" "Six of one, half a dozen of the other. Both are pretty bad."

ctx.s: 两个候选人说得都很好听，可做事都是{半斤八两}。
ctx.en: Both candidates talk a good game, but neither gets any more done than the other.

ctx.s: 吵架这件事，双方都有错，可以说是{半斤八两}。
ctx.en: In this quarrel both sides were in the wrong; there's nothing to choose between them.

ctx.s: 我的英语和他的中文{半斤八两}，聊天全靠手比画。
ctx.en: My English is about as bad as his Chinese, so we chat mostly with our hands.

bad.s: 两位同学都是全校第一名的水平，真是{半斤八两}，太优秀了！
bad.en: (meant: both students are top of the school, equally excellent)
bad.why: It usually implies both are equally poor, so as praise it sounds like a backhanded insult; say bu xiang shang xia.

bad.s: 这块肉大概{半斤八两}，够我们俩吃。
bad.en: (meant: this piece of meat weighs about half a jin, enough for the two of us)
bad.why: It is not used for real weights; it compares two people or things that are no better than each other.

mean: very nearly right, pretty close to the truth
lit: eight or nine, not far from ten

use.how: Predicate or complement after a verb of guessing or judging: 你猜得八九不离十。 Said of a guess, estimate or account that is close to the facts.

near.diff: 差不多 is a general 'about the same, roughly'; 八九不离十 says a guess or judgement is close to the real answer.

cue: Without being told anything, your friend works out almost exactly why you and your boss fell out. How do you admit she has got it about right?

ctx.s: 你猜得{八九不离十}，我确实是想换工作了。
ctx.en: You've guessed pretty much right: I am thinking of changing jobs.

ctx.s: 看他那个表情，我心里就猜了个{八九不离十}：他肯定没考好。
ctx.en: From the look on his face I had a pretty good guess: he hadn't done well in the exam.

ctx.s: “这个包大概多少钱？”“我估计三千块，{八九不离十}。”
ctx.en: "Roughly how much is this bag?" "I'd guess three thousand, give or take."

ctx.s: 他讲的经过虽然有点夸张，但大体上{八九不离十}。
ctx.en: His account of what happened was a bit exaggerated, but broadly it was close to the truth.

ctx.s: 天气预报说明天下雨，最近报得挺准，应该{八九不离十}。
ctx.en: The forecast says rain tomorrow; it's been accurate lately, so it's probably about right.

ctx.s: 警察听完邻居的描述，对嫌疑人身份的判断已经{八九不离十}了。
ctx.en: After hearing the neighbour's description, the police were already close to the truth about who the suspect was.

bad.s: 我们班{八九不离十}的同学都去参加了比赛。
bad.en: (meant: about ninety per cent of our class took part in the contest)
bad.why: It does not mean 'about ninety per cent of'; it judges whether a guess or account is close to the truth.

bad.s: 他{八九不离十}每天都迟到。
bad.en: (meant: he is late almost every day)
bad.why: It is not an adverb of frequency; for 'almost every day' say jihu meitian.

r: dāo zi zuǐ dòu fu xīn
lit: a mouth like a knife and a heart like tofu

use.how: Describes a person, after 是 or as an attributive with 的: 我妈是刀子嘴豆腐心。 Usually said to excuse or explain someone's harsh words.

cue: Your grandmother scolds you loudly for coming home late, then quietly heats up dinner and sits with you while you eat. How do you describe her?

ctx.s: 我妈是{刀子嘴豆腐心}，骂完我又给我煮面。
ctx.en: My mum's bark is worse than her bite: after telling me off she made me noodles.

ctx.s: 别生王老师的气，她就是{刀子嘴豆腐心}。
ctx.en: Don't be angry with Ms Wang; she talks tough, but she has a soft heart.

ctx.s: 老板说话很冲，可大家都知道他{刀子嘴豆腐心}，谁有困难他都帮。
ctx.en: The boss is blunt, but everyone knows he's soft underneath; he helps anyone who's in trouble.

ctx.s: “你奶奶刚才那么凶！”“她{刀子嘴豆腐心}，过一会儿就好了。”
ctx.en: "Your grandma was so fierce just now!" "She sounds harsh but she doesn't mean it; she'll be fine in a minute."

ctx.s: 像他这种{刀子嘴豆腐心}的人，最容易被人误会。
ctx.en: People like him, sharp-tongued but kind at heart, are the easiest to misunderstand.

ctx.s: 爸爸嘴上说不管我了，第二天还是帮我交了房租，真是{刀子嘴豆腐心}。
ctx.en: Dad said he was done with me, but the next day he paid my rent anyway. All talk, soft heart.

bad.s: 他当面对你笑，背后却害你，真是{刀子嘴豆腐心}。
bad.en: (meant: he smiles to your face but stabs you in the back)
bad.why: It is the other way round: harsh words with a kind heart. A sweet face over bad intentions is xiao li cang dao.

bad.s: 她说话总是轻声细语，心地又好，是个{刀子嘴豆腐心}的人。
bad.en: (meant: she is soft-spoken and kind-hearted)
bad.why: The first half needs a sharp tongue; someone gentle in speech and heart is simply kind, not sharp-tongued.

mean: a change in name or form but not in substance
lit: to change the broth but not the medicine in it, as in a herbal decoction

use.how: Predicate, often after 只是、不过是、还是: 新规定不过是换汤不换药。 Criticises reforms, products or plans that look new but are the same.

near.diff: 炒冷饭 repeats old material with nothing new; 换汤不换药 dresses up the old thing to look like a change.

cue: The company renames its overtime policy 'flexible commitment hours', but the hours and pay are exactly the same. What do the staff call it?

ctx.s: 这个新规定只是改了个名字，其实是{换汤不换药}。
ctx.en: The new rule just has a new name; nothing has really changed.

ctx.s: 手机外壳换了个颜色就叫新款，这不是{换汤不换药}吗？
ctx.en: They change the colour of the case and call it a new model. Isn't that the same old thing?

ctx.s: 经理换了三个，管理方式还是老一套，{换汤不换药}。
ctx.en: They've been through three managers, but the management style is the same old stuff: new faces, same thing.

ctx.s: 学校说要减轻学生负担，结果作业从本子上换到了手机上，{换汤不换药}。
ctx.en: The school promised to lighten the students' load, but the homework just moved from exercise books to phones.

ctx.s: 如果只换个口号，制度一点不变，这样的改革就是{换汤不换药}。
ctx.en: If you only swap the slogan and leave the system exactly as it is, the reform is a change in name only.

ctx.s: 这家店重新装修后菜单一点没变，价格倒涨了，顾客都说{换了汤没换药}。
ctx.en: After the refit the menu was exactly the same, only dearer, and customers said it was the same old stuff in new wrapping.

bad.s: 公司彻底改革了管理制度，真是{换汤不换药}，效果非常好！
bad.en: (meant: the company thoroughly reformed its system and it worked very well)
bad.why: It says nothing real has changed, so it cannot describe a thorough reform, and it is always critical.

bad.s: 老店装修得很漂亮，但味道一点没变，{换汤不换药}，太好了！
bad.en: (meant: the old shop got a nice refit and, happily, the food tastes the same)
bad.why: It is a complaint that the change is only on the surface, not praise for keeping what is good.

r: zhēng yī zhī yǎn bì yī zhī yǎn
mean: to turn a blind eye and let something pass
lit: to keep one eye open and one eye shut

use.how: Verb phrase, often 对……睁一只眼闭一只眼. Said of someone who notices a minor fault or rule-breaking and deliberately lets it go.

near.diff: 视而不见 is failing or refusing to see at all; 睁一只眼闭一只眼 is knowing and choosing to let a small thing slide.

cue: The dorm forbids cooking, but the warden knows a student makes noodles in his room every night and never says a word. What is the warden doing?

ctx.s: 小事情就{睁一只眼闭一只眼}吧，别太较真。
ctx.en: Let the little things slide; don't be so strict.

ctx.s: 宿舍不让做饭，可管理员一直对我们{睁一只眼闭一只眼}。
ctx.en: Cooking isn't allowed in the dorm, but the warden has always turned a blind eye to us.

ctx.s: 孩子偶尔多玩一会儿游戏，我也就{睁一只眼闭一只眼}了。
ctx.en: If the kids play video games a bit longer now and then, I just let it go.

ctx.s: “他上班老是晚到十分钟，你不管吗？”“他活干得好，我就{睁只眼闭只眼}。”
ctx.en: "He's always ten minutes late. Aren't you going to do anything?" "His work is good, so I let it pass."

ctx.s: 安全问题不能{睁一只眼闭一只眼}，出了事谁负责？
ctx.en: You can't turn a blind eye to safety problems. If something happens, who'll take responsibility?

ctx.s: 有些地方对小摊小贩{睁一只眼闭一只眼}，反而方便了居民。
ctx.en: Some places look the other way about street stalls, which actually makes life easier for residents.

bad.s: 我当时在看手机，没注意到他进来，{睁一只眼闭一只眼}。
bad.en: (meant: I was on my phone and didn't notice him come in)
bad.why: It means seeing something and choosing to ignore it, not failing to notice it by accident.

bad.s: 监考老师考试时{睁一只眼闭一只眼}，盯得特别紧，谁也别想作弊。
bad.en: (meant: the invigilator watched very closely so no one could cheat)
bad.why: It means the opposite of watching closely: an invigilator who did this would be letting cheating go.

r: bā zì hái méi yī piě
mean: nothing is settled yet, things have barely begun
lit: the character for eight (ba) does not even have its first stroke yet

use.how: Clause, usually 这事八字还没一撇呢. Said to brush off people who talk about a plan, deal or romance as if it were already certain.

cue: You have had one coffee with someone, and your mother is already asking when the wedding is. How do you tell her to calm down?

ctx.s: 结婚？{八字还没一撇}呢，我们才认识一个月。
ctx.en: Getting married? Nothing's settled yet; we've only known each other a month.

ctx.s: 这份工作{八字还没一撇}，你先别告诉别人。
ctx.en: Nothing's certain about this job yet, so don't tell anyone for now.

ctx.s: 项目{八字还没一撇}，他就开始讨论怎么分奖金了。
ctx.en: The project hasn't even got off the ground and he's already talking about how to split the bonus.

ctx.s: “听说你要去国外读书了？”“哪儿啊，申请都没交，{八字还没一撇}。”
ctx.en: "I hear you're going to study abroad?" "Where did you hear that? I haven't even applied. It's nowhere near settled."

ctx.s: 房子的事{八字还没一撇}，装修的样子你倒已经想好了。
ctx.en: Nothing about the flat is settled yet, and you've already planned how to decorate it.

ctx.s: 两家公司合作的事{八字还没一撇}，媒体就已经报道出来了。
ctx.en: Nothing at all had been agreed between the two companies, yet the media was already reporting the partnership.

bad.s: 房子马上就装修好了，{八字还没一撇}。
bad.en: (meant: the flat is almost finished being decorated)
bad.why: It says a matter has barely begun and nothing is settled, the opposite of nearly finished.

bad.s: 人能长生不老吗？我看{八字还没一撇}。
bad.en: (meant: can people live for ever? I think it is impossible)
bad.why: It is about a concrete plan that has not started yet, not about something that can never happen.

r: jī dàn lǐ tiāo gǔ tou
mean: to find fault where there is none
lit: to pick bones out of an egg

use.how: Verb phrase, often 这不是鸡蛋里挑骨头吗 or 专门/故意鸡蛋里挑骨头. Said of someone who invents faults in work or behaviour that is fine.

near.diff: 抬杠 is arguing for the sake of it; 鸡蛋里挑骨头 is inventing faults in something that is fine.

cue: Your report has no errors, so your manager complains that the font looks 'a bit too serious'. What is she doing?

ctx.s: 这篇作文已经很好了，你别{鸡蛋里挑骨头}。
ctx.en: This essay is already very good; stop looking for faults that aren't there.

ctx.s: 新来的主管专门{鸡蛋里挑骨头}，大家都怕交报告给他。
ctx.en: The new supervisor goes out of his way to find fault, so everyone dreads handing him reports.

ctx.s: 菜做得好好的，他非说盘子颜色不对，这不是{鸡蛋里挑骨头}吗？
ctx.en: The food was perfectly good and he insisted the plates were the wrong colour. Isn't that nitpicking for nothing?

ctx.s: “这条裙子的扣子好像有点歪。”“哪儿歪了？你就是在{鸡蛋里挑骨头}。”
ctx.en: "The buttons on this dress look a bit crooked." "Crooked where? You're just looking for something to complain about."

ctx.s: 婆婆看她什么都不顺眼，连她叠衣服的方法都要{鸡蛋里挑出骨头}来。
ctx.en: Her mother-in-law disapproves of everything she does and even finds fault with the way she folds clothes.

ctx.s: 审稿要认真，但也不能{鸡蛋里挑骨头}，把作者的风格都改没了。
ctx.en: Editing should be careful, but you shouldn't invent faults and edit the author's style out of existence.

bad.s: 报告里错字很多，经理{鸡蛋里挑骨头}，把它们都找了出来。
bad.en: (meant: the report had many typos and the manager found them all)
bad.why: It means finding faults that do not exist; pointing out real errors is just careful checking.

bad.s: 我弟弟吃饭{鸡蛋里挑骨头}，这个不吃那个也不吃。
bad.en: (meant: my brother is a picky eater)
bad.why: It is about inventing criticism, not about food; a picky eater is tiaoshi.

r: dǎ kāi tiān chuāng shuō liàng huà
mean: to speak frankly and openly, hiding nothing
lit: to open the skylight and speak in the light

use.how: Said by the speaker before getting blunt, often 咱们打开天窗说亮话吧 or 我就打开天窗说亮话了. Signals dropping politeness to say what both sides really think.

near.diff: 开门见山 is getting straight to the point in speech or writing; 打开天窗说亮话 is dropping pretence in a tense conversation.

cue: After an hour of polite hints in a pay negotiation, you decide to stop pretending and tell the other side your real bottom line. What do you say first?

ctx.s: 咱们{打开天窗说亮话}吧，你到底想要多少钱？
ctx.en: Let's be frank: exactly how much money do you want?

ctx.s: 既然你问了，那我就{打开天窗说亮话}，这个方案我不同意。
ctx.en: Since you ask, I'll be blunt: I don't agree with this plan.

ctx.s: 都是老朋友了，有什么不满就{打开天窗说亮话}，别憋在心里。
ctx.en: We're old friends; if something's bothering you, out with it, don't keep it bottled up.

ctx.s: “您的意思是……”“我{打开天窗说亮话}，公司今年不打算给你升职。”
ctx.en: "So what you mean is..." "I'll put it plainly: the company doesn't plan to promote you this year."

ctx.s: 谈判拖了一上午，最后双方决定{打开天窗说亮话}，很快就签了合同。
ctx.en: The talks dragged on all morning; in the end both sides decided to lay their cards on the table and soon signed.

ctx.s: 与其互相猜来猜去，不如{打开天窗说亮话}，把问题解决了。
ctx.en: Rather than second-guessing each other, we'd do better to speak openly and sort the problem out.

bad.s: 后面的同学听不清，请你{打开天窗说亮话}。
bad.en: (meant: the students at the back can't hear, please speak up)
bad.why: It is about speaking frankly, not loudly; to ask someone to speak up say da sheng dian.

bad.s: 她{打开天窗说亮话}，把好朋友的秘密告诉了全班。
bad.en: (meant: she blurted out her best friend's secret to the whole class)
bad.why: It is candour between the speaker and listener about their own matter, not leaking someone else's secret.

r: guà yáng tóu mài gǒu ròu
mean: to pass off something inferior under a respectable label
lit: to hang up a sheep's head and sell dog meat

story.text: Duke Ling of Qi liked the women of his palace to dress as men. The fashion spread through the state, so he banned it outside the palace, but the ban did not work. His minister Yanzi told him: you let them do it inside and forbid it outside; that is like hanging an ox head at the door and selling horse meat inside. Stop it in the palace and no one outside will dare. The Duke did, and the fashion ended. Later the saying took its present form, with a sheep's head and dog meat.

use.how: Predicate or attributive: 这家公司挂羊头卖狗肉。 Exposes businesses, organisations or people that use a good name to sell or do something quite different and worse.

near.diff: 换汤不换药 is a cosmetic change to the same old thing; 挂羊头卖狗肉 is a respectable front hiding something worse.

cue: A shop advertised as a 'health and wellness centre' turns out to be selling dubious pills at huge prices to elderly people. How do you expose it?

ctx.s: 这家店说卖进口牛肉，其实是便宜货，{挂羊头卖狗肉}。
ctx.en: This shop claims to sell imported beef, but it's cheap stuff: a classic bait and switch.

ctx.s: 那个所谓的英语培训班根本不上课，就是{挂羊头卖狗肉}，推销保健品。
ctx.en: That so-called English course never holds classes; it's just a front for selling health supplements.

ctx.s: 有些网站{挂着学术的羊头卖广告的狗肉}，读者要小心。
ctx.en: Some websites put on an academic front but are really selling ads, so readers should be careful.

ctx.s: “这个纪录片怎么全是产品介绍？”“它就是{挂羊头卖狗肉}的广告。”
ctx.en: "Why is this documentary all product plugs?" "It's an advert dressed up as something respectable."

ctx.s: 记者调查发现，这家“养老服务中心”{挂羊头卖狗肉}，专门骗老人买高价药。
ctx.en: Reporters found that this 'elderly care centre' was a front, set up to trick old people into buying overpriced medicine.

ctx.s: 做生意要讲诚信，{挂羊头卖狗肉}的做法早晚会被发现。
ctx.en: Business needs honesty; passing off rubbish under a good name will be found out sooner or later.

bad.s: 这家店{挂羊头卖狗肉}，卖的都是正宗的新疆羊肉，很好吃。
bad.en: (meant: this shop sells genuine, delicious Xinjiang lamb)
bad.why: It accuses a seller of deceiving customers, so it cannot praise a shop that sells exactly what it advertises.

bad.s: 这家饭馆{挂羊头卖狗肉}，菜单上什么肉都有，选择很多。
bad.en: (meant: this restaurant serves all kinds of meat and has a wide choice)
bad.why: It is only figurative, about a fake front hiding something worse, never a description of a varied menu.
